title: Also this show is SO loud- I highly recommend bringing some ear plugs...
transcript: This is maybe one of the most bizarre theater experiences I've ever had, because I've never had such a disconnect between the show that I was watching and experiencing and the show that everyone else around me was watching and experiencing. And this is probably largely a generational thing, because the people around me were all older. They were people that have probably grown up on this musical, on the album, on the movie, and had some level of nostalgia for this material. But for me, apart from Pinball Wizard being performed on Glee, this was really my first exposure to this source material. And I was warned that the show is really weird, that the plot doesn't really make sense. And I was ready for that, but I was not ready for how uncomfortable I would be while watching the show. To the show's credit, I do think a lot of what happens in the show is supposed to be uncomfortable. It's supposed to be a commentary on the way in which society, um, treats disabled people, which is to say, not very well. But at the same time, there was a real dissonance between me feeling uncomfortable with what was going on at stage and everyone around me bopping along and enjoying the fun rock score and, like, having a good time. Which kind of only made me more uncomfortable, because I was like, well, are they, like, missing what's going on on stage? Are they missing this Messaging. And there were a lot of times where my discomfort just kept me from actively enjoying the piece that I was watching. Like, I think the Acid Queen scene is a great example of that, because, like, Christina Sodus is giving an amazing performance with these killer vocals, but I'm not really able to enjoy them because what's happening in the scene is so deeply fucked up. Like, you're watching this father sell off his young child, who is disabled, to a woman of the night in hopes of curing that child of that disability. Like, deeply fucked up. Meanwhile, everyone around me in the audience is just, like, bopping along to The Acid Queen, the song that they, I guess, know and love and having a grand old time. And that was kind of how I felt for a majority of the show. And I didn't feel like act to really reckoned with any of the fucked up things that happened in Act 1 in any way. That was satisfying. I do get the appeal to some extent. I do think the music is really good. I think the cast for this revival is really, really great. The show itself is just not for me, and I don't know that it holds up. Andre Modern Lens. I'm gonna give it a two out of five stars, with the caveat that, like, if you already know, and like, Tommy, I think you're gonna like this production. But if you're Someone that does not know Tommy. I would say at least read the Wikipedia first to know what you're getting into.
